Claude Code推出实验性Code Mode：一次调用多个工具，长任务可后台执行

Anthropic 为 Claude Code 加入实验性 Code Mode，已在 11 月 12 日发布的 v2.1.323 中上线，目前需要手动开启。

启用后，Claude 可以先编写 JavaScript 脚本，再通过脚本连续、并行调用多个工具，还能把工具返回的数据先处理好，只将必要结果交给模型，从而减少模型请求和 Token 消耗。

新模式还支持长时间任务在后台运行。Claude 可以一边执行命令，一边继续回答用户。官方文档显示，后台脚本最长可运行 2 小时，但需要使用 Auto 等自动授权模式。

Code Mode 由 Cloudflare 于 2025 年 9 月提出，Anthropic 同年 11 月也公开了类似方案。今年，DeepSeek Harness、Pi 和 OpenCode 2.0 等开源 Agent 框架陆续加入支持。

Anthropic 如今才将其集成进 Claude Code，目前仍处于实验阶段，需要手动开启。

OpenAI董事长创办的AI客服公司，半年估值拟翻倍至300亿美元

OpenAI 董事长、Salesforce 前联席 CEO Bret Taylor 创办的 AI 客服公司 Sierra，正洽谈融资约 15 亿美元，目标估值高达 300 亿美元。

Lightspeed、Greenoaks 和 Benchmark 正考虑投资，谈判仍处于早期。Sierra 今年 5 月刚以 158 亿美元估值融资 9.5 亿美元。仅过半年，估值就有望接近翻倍。

Sierra 成立于 2023 年，专门帮企业部署 AI 客服。它的智能体不仅能接听电话、回答问题，还能连接企业内部系统，处理退款、订单变更等事务。客户包括摩根大通、Cigna 等大型企业，部分业务按 AI 成功解决的问题收费。

它的收入增长也很快。Sierra 今年 10 月披露，年化经常性收入（ARR）已超过 4 亿美元，短短 5 个月翻了一倍。仅第三季度就新增超过 1.5 亿美元。按目前披露的收入规模计算，300 亿美元估值约相当于 ARR 的 75 倍。

竞争对手 Decagon 也在筹备新一轮数亿美元融资，其今年第二季度末年化收入约 1 亿美元，预计年底达到 1.75 亿至 2 亿美元。

OpenAI推出ChatGPT会计工作台：接入8款插件，帮企业对账、做报表

OpenAI 推出 ChatGPT for Accounting，发布专门的 Accounting 插件，并接入 QuickBooks、Xero、Oracle NetSuite、BILL 等 8 款合作插件，让 ChatGPT 可以直接读取企业账目，协助处理发票、银行对账、月末结账和审计准备工作。

过去，会计人员需要从邮箱、银行和财务软件中分别查找资料，再手工整理核对。现在，ChatGPT 可以汇集发票、银行流水和付款记录，识别交易金额、建议记账科目，再与账本逐笔核对，找出重复记账、遗漏交易及金额不符等问题。

到了月底，AI 还能按照企业原有的 Excel 模板编制财务报告，分析收入、支出等数据的变化，并附上对应的原始记录，方便会计人员核查。常用的报表格式、记账规则和检查步骤也可以保存下来，下个月继续使用。

Slack要做企业AI的指挥中心：让Agent接管任务，员工负责审核

Slack 宣布整合 Workflow Builder、Slackbot 和第三方 AI Agent，进一步将团队聊天工具升级为企业 AI 工作中枢。员工无需编写代码，就能在 Slack 中安排 AI 执行任务，并把处理结果接入现有业务流程。

比如员工提交 VPN 故障工单后，工作流可以直接唤起 IT Agent，带着问题继续排查。客户消息被标记后，Slackbot 能自动总结问题、起草回复。AI 生成的内容还可以经过人工审核，再写入 Jira、Google Sheets 或 Salesforce。

第三方 Agent 也有了自己的定时任务功能。用户只需保存一次指令，就能让已接入 Slack 的 Agent 每周自动整理销售机会、分析数据或生成报告，无需额外开发调度程序。

豆包音视频通话模型开放API：AI能边看边听边说，还会主动开口

11 月 19 日，火山引擎正式开放豆包实时音视频模型 SeedRealtime 1.0 的 API。该模型今年 8 月就已在豆包 App 上线，如今第三方开发者也能将这套实时视频通话能力接入自己的产品。

SeedRealtime 将摄像头画面、声音和时间顺序放进同一个端到端模型。AI 可以一边观察、一边听用户说话，同时判断该什么时候开口，减少传统语音识别、视觉理解、语音合成等多个模块串联带来的延迟和信息损失。

官方演示中，用户把整颗咖啡豆倒进咖啡机的萃取手柄，AI 不等提问就主动提醒先研磨。逛博物馆时，用户只需提前交代要找哪件文物，模型便能持续观察镜头，在目标出现时主动提醒。它还能分辨多人对话，在嘈杂环境中避免被旁人的闲聊误触发。

字节跳动今年 8 月公布的人工评测显示，相比多个模型串联的方案，SeedRealtime 的音视频对话节奏问题减少约一半，抢话、回应迟缓和背景噪声误触发等现象明显减少。

#buybuybuy #Life #Car #Blog

🛞 换胎胜似换新车：All in 米其林 PS5

🔗：Blog

🛒 购买渠道：米其林天猫官方旗舰店
💰 价格：约 1133 元/条（淘金币抵扣）

上两周，不小心将前保险杠铲到水泥牙子上，轮胎“咻”的一声裂了一个口，去年刚换的 PS5 就这么报废掉了。好在京东提供了按购买价格的 80% 赔偿方案，总算挽回了大半损失。（😭

正好后轮原配的固特异已经跑了 4 万 5 公里，磨损快到安全线了，干脆一并换掉，毫无疑问，这次依旧选择米其林 PS5，相比轮胎的固特异鹰驰 F1，胎噪小了不少，高速上过积水路面很平稳，不容易打滑，还有米其林“随你行”的质保托底。除了性能，米其林 PS5 胎壁的耀黑工艺颜值很高，搭配全黑车身，让爱车的外观更炫酷。

可惜的是，米其林新出的 PS5E 还没有 245/40 R19 的规格，静音棉的加入，座舱静谧性还能再上一个台阶，PS5E 的滚阻评级也优于 PS5，降低行驶的能耗。

换完轮胎，我特地去跑了趟盘山公路，试着把直道和过弯速度提到了 70-80 km/h，能感受到扎实的抓地力，过弯时的指向性更精准，让人在高速、城市道路紧急变线更有信心，对整车的操控信心都提升不少。

那 PS5 有什么缺点吗？这款轮胎属于性能驾驶取向，C 级高滚阻带来了强抓地力与操控能力，代价是更高的油耗与电耗。另外，静音表现与滤震能力无法媲美静音舒适型轮胎，平整沥青路面还能接受，但上了水泥路、碎石路与高速，胎噪和车内细碎的异响变得十分明显，只有用更大的音乐声掩盖。

另外提一嘴，想要享受米其林“随你行”权益，轮胎需要从官方渠道购买，京东自营、途虎渠道购买的轮胎，依赖平台售后。我这次是从米其林天猫官方旗舰店，可以使用淘金币抵扣，攒了几万的淘金币终于派上用场，算下来价格比京东自营划算不少。

总体来说，从去年用到现在，换米其林是个很值得的选择，整体表现完全对得起它的价格，雨天跑高速能稳稳当当地过积水路面，跑山路上又能给足驾驶乐趣（乘客除外）。日常开着踏实，偶尔开快点也不慌。正如 PS5 的描述，Precision and driving pleasure for more miles.

📱 德奥两国提议 TikTok 欧洲业务转为欧洲所有

德国和奥地利提议要求 TikTok 将欧洲业务交由欧洲所有者持有，称此举有助于保护个人数据、增强欧洲自主权并应对安全风险。

两国希望争取其他欧洲国家支持，方案尚未列入讨论议程；若 TikTok 不自愿出售，强制出售也需要欧盟委员会支持。TikTok 发言人称该提议“毫无道理”。

Google’s water stewardship commitments for local communities

Learn about our water commitments and initiatives.

Ben Townsend

Head of Infrastructure & Sustainability

Listen to article

[[duration]] minutes

This content is generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental

Data centers are the nerve centers of the digital world, powering our daily lives with Search, Maps, online banking, healthcare and 911 systems. As we grow our data center footprint to support these services, we recognize that how we build is just as important as what we build.

Water is a critical component of data center development and operations. Because data centers generate heat from the servers and chips that power the digital world, they often rely on water to cut back on energy use for cooling. In many places, water cooling can reduce data center energy use by approximately 10% compared to air cooling. The aggregate water consumption of data centers is small — U.S. data centers use less than 1% of the water that Americans use on their lawns annually

1
— but we are focused on protecting local water resources in all aspects of our data center operations.

We are committed to responsibly manage vital water resources where we build and operate data centers. Our goal is to minimize our local impacts so that our growth does not come at the expense of the communities we call home. We’re also announcing new water stewardship initiatives and evaluating projects through Google’s water replenishment Request for Information (RFI).

New water stewardship commitments

Under these five commitments, Google will:

1. Replenish more water than we consume at our sites
2
by 2030. By investing in replenishment projects, we can help improve water security for everyone. In 2025, we replenished more than 7 billion gallons (roughly equivalent to the annual water usage of 70,000 average U.S. households).

3
And, as of 2025, we have 165 water stewardship projects across 97 watersheds. Once these projects are fully implemented, they are expected to replenish more than 19 billion gallons of water annually by 2030, more than double our 2024 consumption (enough water to supply the entire city of Los Angeles for more than 40 days). The majority of these projects not only deliver volumetric benefits, but also help improve broader watershed health challenges such as water quality.

2. Help modernize water and wastewater infrastructure for our neighbors. Water utilities are often underfunded. By working with our utility partners, we are helping update public water infrastructure so that our neighbors have reliable, affordable water sources both today and in the future. In addition to paying for the water we use, to date Google has committed over $500 million to the development of water, wastewater and water reuse infrastructure and to the utility partners that deliver water in the communities where we operate/build data centers. This includes projects ranging from enhancing local water supplies to detecting leaky pipes. We’re committed to continuing to help local utilities update their infrastructure.

3. Protect at-risk watersheds with air-cooled solutions. We use a data-driven framework to assess local watersheds for new data centers before we build, and only consider water cooling if local resources are healthy and resilient. If a water source is at high risk, we choose air cooling or recycled water. We will continue to work in partnership with state agencies and local utilities to follow these principles and ensure our approach reflects community needs.

4. Report our annual water use transparently. Water use shouldn’t be a “black box.” Google was the first major cloud provider to disclose our annual water use for our data center locations, and we’re committed to continuing to do so to ensure transparency for the communities where we invest and build.

5. Pursue alternative and reclaimed solutions to protect water resources. We are working with utility partners to identify freshwater alternatives at our data centers, such as reclaimed wastewater. A prime example is in Douglas County, Georgia, where we partnered with the county’s water and sewer authority to reuse treated wastewater for cooling at our data center campus.

Google’s water replenishment RFI

To further our replenishment goals, we’re also evaluating more than 700 projects submitted through our recent Water Replenishment Projects RFI. These projects include engineered solutions to improve water efficiency, supply or quality; farm-level practices to reduce agricultural water demand and improve soil health; and nature-based solutions aimed at improving the hydrologic cycle. We’ll have more to share in the coming months as we work with partners to roll out these projects.

Water is an essential natural resource that communities work hard to conserve. Through our water stewardship commitments, we will continue to be responsible and transparent in our water use — protecting the long-term health of the watersheds in communities we call home.

New water stewardship initiatives

Last updated: November 19, 2026

Our commitment to water stewardship has grown significantly. This year, we've announced over $100 million in funding to support community water sources, infrastructure, and access in 14 states. Here’s a list of our latest water stewardship initiatives, and we’ll be updating this list on an ongoing basis.

• Arkansas: Ducks Unlimited to support key park amenities at Ducks Unlimited Park, bringing learning and interactive program opportunities to children and other park visitors across the Mid-South.

• Arizona: Trout Unlimited and the US Fish and Wildlife Service to remove and replace culverts that will restore natural streamflow and reconnect vital habitats for the Apache Trout.

• Georgia: Ducks Unlimited to enhance wetlands at the Flint River Wildlife Management Area.

• Indiana: Fort Wayne City Utilities to optimize water reuse at its water treatment plant, reducing withdrawals from the St. Joseph River.

• Iowa:The Great Outdoors Foundation and the Iowa Department of Agriculture and Land Stewardship to help local farmers in Western Iowa convert 5,000 acres into perennial hay and pasture systems, reducing fertilizer use and improving water quality.Bur Oak Land Trust to acquire and convert a 165-acre property adjacent to the Corriell Nature Preserve into managed wetlands and prairies to enhance natural infiltration and recharge.

• Michigan: Huron River Watershed Council to expand its green infrastructure program, using native plantings to treat stormwater and mitigate flooding.

• Minnesota: Trust for Public Land to restore 84 acres of floodplain forest, establishing a 1-mile corridor along the Zumbro River to improve water quality.

• Missouri: Bridging the Gap and the Heartland Conservation Alliance to restore 98 acres adjacent to the Blue River as a wetland, improving water quality and providing critical habitat.

• Nebraska: The Metropolitan Utilities District’s water line leak detection program in Omaha to help reduce water loss and improve system efficiency.

• Ohio: Department of Agriculture’s H2Ohio Farmland Water Management Program to optimize drainage structures to reduce agricultural runoff and conserve water.

• Oklahoma: Oklahoma Conservation Commission to remove invasive, water-intensive Eastern Red Cedar trees and restore cropland to native playa wetlands in the panhandle.

• South Carolina: National Audubon Society to construct nature-based features, specifically berms, that will protect wetlands and their corresponding habitat in the Cape Romain National Wildlife Refuge.

• Texas: Funding to support community water sources, infrastructure, and access across the state.

• Virginia:Frog Creek Partners to improve water quality throughout Virginia’s Chesapeake Bay and Roanoke River watersheds by installing stormwater filtration systems.The Virginia Association of Soil and Water Conservation Districts (VASWCD) to reduce the quantity and improve the water quality of stormwater runoff entering natural waterways across public, private, and Tribal lands.Ducks Unlimited to support the enhancement of approximately 60 acres of wetlands at the Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources James River and Dick Cross Wildlife Management Areas, as well as support the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service’s efforts in restoring tidal, freshwater wetland dynamics within the Elizabeth Hartwell Mason Neck National Wildlife Refuge.ION Water to support the deployment of their End-to-End Water Management system across approximately 4,500 affordable housing units in Northern Virginia and the Metro DC area.

Linq获a16z领投9000万美元：让AI接短信、打电话、操作电脑，估值达10亿美元

AI 智能体基础设施公司 Linq 宣布完成 a16z 领投的 9000 万美元 B 轮融资，估值达到 10 亿美元。a16z 联合创始人 Ben Horowitz 加入董事会。今年 2 月，Linq 才刚完成 2000 万美元 A 轮融资。

Linq 的核心业务，是让 AI 像普通联系人一样出现在手机里。用户不用下载专门的 App，就能通过 iMessage、短信或 WhatsApp 与 AI 交流。开发者则通过 Linq 的接口，把自己的 AI 智能体接入这些聊天渠道。

目前，DoorDash 已利用 Linq，让顾客直接在苹果的商务消息中选餐、加入购物车并结账，全程无需离开聊天窗口。Linq 称，其客户累计已通过平台处理超过 10 亿条消息。

Linq 还推出了 HD Calling，让 AI 可以直接拨打、接听高清电话，并与短信服务打通，无需依赖第三方电话服务。同时提供托管的 Mac mini，让 AI 远程操作浏览器和 macOS 软件。浏览器基础设施公司 Kernel 已成为首批客户之一。

Linq 还成为苹果官方认证的 Messages for Business 服务提供商，可以帮助企业接入苹果商务消息。

items.body:
OpenAI让AI改进AMD旗舰GPU：5个月推进约1年的优化，部分成果已送厂制造

OpenAI 不光向 AMD 采购 GPU，现在还让自己的 AI 帮 AMD 改进芯片设计。

AMD 的旗舰 GPU 电路已经由工程师反复优化多年，但 OpenAI 的模型仍找到了最高 14% 的改进空间。OpenAI 称，双方在不到 5 个月内，完成了通常需要约一年才能取得的优化进展。

AI 会直接修改描述芯片电路的代码，尝试更高效的计算和数据传输方式，再调用专业软件验证功能是否正确、功耗和性能有没有改善。AMD 已将部分修改用于最近送厂制造的芯片设计，其余成果也被纳入后续产品。

OpenAI 在开发自研推理芯片 Jalapeño 时，就已经让 AI 参与电路设计。这次与 AMD 的合作证明，即使是经验丰富的工程师反复优化过的芯片，AI 也能找到新的改进方案，并被实际用于产品设计。

Anthropic或让4250名员工跻身百万富翁，财富开始涌向旧金山房市和奢侈品

Anthropic 正式敲定每股 83 美元的 IPO 发行价。未上市公司股票交易平台 Hill 之前估算，这次上市可能让约 4250 名员工成为百万美元富翁，占公司约 5300 名员工的 80%。其中约 1200 人持股价值超过 1000 万美元，50 人超过 1 亿美元。

旧金山的高端房地产市场已经升温。今年已有超过 210 套住宅以高出挂牌价至少 100 万美元的价格成交。AI 行业持续造富，也让当地市场开始期待更多科技新贵入场。

奢侈腕表市场同样火热。交易平台 Bezel 的 CEO Quaid Walker 透露，今年该平台在旧金山的销售额同比翻倍，两年增长约七倍。当地买家平均每笔消费达到 14,350 美元，比其他地区高约 2000 美元。其中 14% 的订单超过 2.5 万美元，比例是其他地区的两倍。

Walker 预计，随着 Anthropic 等 AI 公司员工陆续兑现股权，这批新富豪会把更多钱花在豪宅、稀有腕表和其他难以复制的奢侈品上。

韩国AI作弊风波升级：满分学霸直播自证前身亡，警方调查或将终止

11 月 19 日，韩国法学研究生入学考试（LEET）史上首位满分考生李振宇（32 岁），在首尔一家旅馆被发现身亡。

当天上午，他原本打算在媒体面前直播解答韩国高考语文试题，以证明自己的真实水平，回应 AI 作弊质疑，但最终没有现身。

李振宇曾自述，自己早年高考成绩只有第 6 至 8 等级（韩国实行九级制，数字越大成绩越差），后来却考入首尔大学牙科学院。今年 7 月，他又答对 LEET 全部 70 道题，成为这项考试自 2008 年设立以来首个满分考生。

争议来自他此前公开的一份试卷。其中连续 3 道题的涂改前答案，恰好对应上一道题的正确选项。网友怀疑，他可能在抄录外部提供的答案时发生错位。

韩国另一名税务师考试状元此前已承认，自己通过微型摄像头拍摄试题，再利用 AI 获取答案。这起案件让李振宇受到更多质疑。李振宇则坚决否认作弊，称试卷反复涂改是因为考试后半段注意力下降。

11 月 18 日，多名律师正式向警方举报李振宇。次日，他未能出席公开验证，随后被发现身亡。警方在现场找到疑似遗书的便条，内容提到身心疲惫，但没有承认作弊。目前具体死亡原因仍在调查。

由于当事人死亡，针对他的刑事调查预计将终止。不过，韩国教育部门已要求保留他此前参加高考的答卷，是否进一步调查作弊疑云尚未确定。

items.title: How OpenAI’s Performance Factory keeps ChatGPT fast
items.summary: Learn how OpenAI built the Performance Factory, a system of Codex-powered workflows that finds and fixes performance issues to help keep ChatGPT fast.
items.body:
November 19, 2026

Engineering

Our Codex-powered system automates finding and fixing performance issues.

By Okay Zed and Cyrus Forbes, Members of Technical Staff

The staggering pace of agentic development has made traditional approaches to performance engineering unsustainable. To keep up, we built the Performance Factory, an autonomous system that uses the full capabilities of Codex and our models to find and fix regressions at an unprecedented speed. The Performance Factory, which runs in the cloud and automates investigating and resolving performance problems, enables us to keep pace with the ambition of our roadmap.

In the Performance Factory, our engineers define workflows for recurring jobs and write instructions for the Codex agents that carry them out. In particular, the Regression Workflow opens a task when a performance alert fires. An agent investigates the slowdown, records its findings in the task, and proposes a fix for an engineer to review. After deployment, another agent picks up the same task to check whether performance has returned to baseline. From investigating to authoring the fix to verifying mitigation, this first workflow in the Performance Factory has automated the entire process of fixing regressions. In just over three months, the Regression Workflow tracked more than 1,700 investigations and root caused over 600 cases. That’s 17 automated investigations every day.

Here, we’ll share how our use of Codex evolved into what’s now the Performance Factory, walk through our first running workflow, and share early lessons from building and running agent workflows in production.

As we used Codex for more of our performance work, we noticed a progression in how our team worked. We hope other service teams can learn from our process as they adopt agentic workflows in other domains.

1. Pre-Codex. Before Codex, engineers manually examined metrics and logs, compared traces, debugged live machines, and read code to investigate a slowdown. This work was time consuming, and knowing where to look often required deep knowledge of the service. Relevant signals were easy to miss. When we encountered the same kinds of problems repeatedly—like regressions in ChatGPT’s first token latency—we built advanced tools, like CPU and allocation profilers, to make those investigations easier. Over time, we accumulated more than 30 performance tools.

2. Codex as a partner. Once we had Codex as a partner, engineers could ask, “Why did this get slower?” and work with Codex to investigate, even in an unfamiliar system. Codex could search large codebases, find relevant metrics and traces, follow interactions across services, and do appropriate profiling to piece together what had happened. But engineers still had to steer the process, knowing which performance tools to use and how to guide the investigation. Difficult investigations were more debuggable for more people, with less expertise and time required.

3. Reusable skills. To automate further, we captured our performance team’s investigation process in a shared skill called perf-forensics. It tells Codex which tools are available, when to use them, and how to work through a slowdown so Codex can try to resolve the problem from a few angles:

• Find when the slowdown began

• Identify the affected requests

• Investigate whether deployments or configuration changes could explain it

We tested and refined the perf-forensics skill using evals based on past regressions. For the types of regressions we focused on (for example, ChatGPT latency and availability drops), we could now give Codex an alert and get back a diagnosis in a single run, without guiding it through each step.

4. The human proxy. As we added and refined perf-related Codex skills like perf-forensics, we started to feel like a proxy between our alerts and Codex. An alert would fire, and an engineer would simply copy and paste it into Codex with the right skill, then paste the findings back into Slack.

5. Automated investigations. Next, we moved investigations to the cloud so an alert could start a Codex session automatically. Codex investigated the slowdown and posted its findings in the Slack thread, but the automation ended with that reply. An engineer still had to pick up the diagnosis, develop a fix, and check whether it worked after deployment. As alerts accumulated, even figuring out which regressions needed attention meant sifting through Slack threads.

6. The factory. We built the Performance Factory to run end-to-end agentic performance engineering workflows. It tracks what each active task needs next and assigns an agent when that step is ready. Each task keeps its state and findings, so work can pass between agents and engineers and resume after a code review or deployment. For a regression, the work starts with investigating an alert and ends with verifying recovery in production. We can turn common optimizations into workflows that run regularly across our services. A workflow that spots a potential optimization can open a task in another workflow to test and implement it.

The Performance Factory is made up of four components: a task tracker with configurable workflows, a dispatch loop that assigns ready work to agents, an API that runs Codex in the cloud, and subscriptions that wake agents when something changes (such as a GitHub review comment posting or a deployment completing).

The task service is where engineers define workflows by adding configuration files and prompts for the agents to follow, written in Markdown. The configuration lists the states a task can move through, the allowed transitions, and which steps need an engineer. Separate prompts tell agents what to do at each step.

Plain text

1code-change/2├── config.toml3└── work/4    ├── implementing.md5    └── reviewing.md

A code change task contains a configuration file, along with Markdown prompts for implementing and reviewing.

Each piece of work becomes a task in a workflow, and all workflows are visible in a UI. Engineers can see what’s open, follow progress, and share a task with a teammate who might have more context or be able to help with the next step.

A dispatch loop periodically checks which tasks are ready for the next step. It assigns an agent to each task by starting a Codex turn with the instructions for the task’s current state. The agent records its progress on the task and moves it to the next state if it completes the step.

Once a task is assigned, the agent needs a place to do the work, with access to the same tools an engineer would use. We built an internal API to programmatically invoke a Codex turn in the cloud. The Codex turn runs on an environment inside our network, with access to our code repositories and the observability tools our engineers use, such as metrics, logs, traces, CPU profiles, and memory snapshots.

The agent runs under a service identity, so we can scope its permissions and see which actions came from our performance agents. Moving agentic work to the cloud lets us run work in parallel without relying on engineers’ laptops being open or manually managing individual cloud development boxes.

Some work has to wait for a person or a deployment; an agent shouldn’t have to keep running in the meantime. When a task needs to wait, it can subscribe to events like review comments or failed CI checks on a GitHub pull request to get notified when it’s time to pick the work back up. When an incoming event matches the subscription, the task becomes ready again and the dispatch loop can then assign an agent to continue the work.

Finding, root causing, and solving regressions is the first workflow we built inside the Performance Factory. We call it the Regression Workflow. A performance regression moves through several stages: needs investigation, root caused, fix proposed, and resolved, so we built the automated workflow to reflect and move a task through those same stages.

When one of its configured performance alerts fires, the Regression Workflow opens a task that agents pick up and move across these stages. The task records its status and key findings outside of any one agent’s context so that other agents or engineers can pick up the work. Engineers can follow the work in Slack or the Regression Workflow UI, add context, and review proposed changes. After a fix is deployed, an agent checks whether the performance has recovered to its original state before resolving the task.

Finding the root cause (or causes) is the first major step in the workflow. The agent starts by figuring out which metrics got worse, when they started to change, and which service requests were affected. The perf-forensics skill gives Codex access to the tools our performance engineers use and a playbook for working through those questions.

An alert fires when a metric crosses a threshold, but the regression may have started hours earlier. The agent looks back through the data to find when the metric first got worse. It then compares groups of requests: did similar requests actually get slower, or were we serving more requests that were already slow? Those findings point to different causes.

Once it knows when and where to look, the agent examines deployments and feature flag changes, then reads the relevant code. It checks when a change actually reached the affected requests and uses logs or traces to test whether the code could explain what happened.

Early on, agents sometimes stopped at the first plausible explanation they found, and some of those diagnoses turned out to be wrong. To catch these mistakes, we added an adversarial review: a separate Codex session that tries to disprove the proposed diagnosis. The reviewer rechecks the assumptions and tests counterfactuals. If a rollout caused the slowdown, did similar requests that weren’t exposed stay healthy? If the suspected change was rolled back, did the affected metric recover?

In one investigation, an agent traced failing ChatGPT conversations to errors in image downloads and marked the cause as found. The Codex reviewer noticed that the internal service responsible for locating files had already recovered while image requests were still failing. The diagnosis did not explain the continuing failures, so the AI reviewer reopened the investigation and recorded what still needed to be established.

We’ve had success breaking larger jobs into focused Codex turns. In a manual review of 100 root cause suggestions, we graded 70% as accurate, with 30% needing further refinement or not fully establishing causality. In the Regression Workflow, different turns investigate regressions, challenge diagnoses, and propose fixes to increase accuracy numbers through checks and balances.

Once the diagnosis passes adversarial review, the workflow asks Codex to implement a fix and open a pull request. An engineer reviews the PR and decides whether to merge it. We’ve put a significant amount of work into making this handoff as easy as possible. Each task has a report with an automatically generated summary of the regression, its impact, the root cause, and the proposed fix. Cloudflare重做信息提取模型Clairic：从9B升级27B，新增PDF识别并开源

Cloudflare 发布新版信息提取模型 Clairic，并推出轻量版 Clairic-flash。两款模型分别基于 Qwen3.8-27B 和 Qwen3.5-9B 开发，均已开源模型权重及推理代码，采用 Apache 2.0 许可证。

Clairic 此前于 10 月推出 9B 预览版，主要用于从文字、图片中提取金额、日期、订单号等数据，也能进行简单计算和预测。这次主模型升级至 27B，新增 PDF 识别，最多可同时处理 4 页 PDF 或图片，还能更准确地识别表格、清单等复杂内容。

Cloudflare 还重新设计了信息提取方式。旧版一次计算就给出结果，新版允许多个字段并行逐步生成答案，以少量速度损失换取更高准确率。

官方自测中，在包含文字和图片的合成收据测试里，旧版正确提取了 576 个字段中的 369 个，新版则全部答对。9B 的 Clairic-flash 在同一测试中也全部答对，处理普通文本字段的中位延迟约为 155 毫秒，27B 版则为 358 毫秒。

两款模型现已上线 Workers AI，12 月 1 日前均按每百万输入 Token 0.10 美元收费。此后 27B 版涨至 0.24 美元，9B 版维持 0.10 美元，均不收取输出 Token 费用。

11 月 18 日，英伟达临时 CEO Colette Kress 在黄仁勋辞职后的首次全员大会上，呼吁员工「向前看」，同时宣布将加薪和额外股票奖励提前至今年 12 月，比原定时间早了数月。

员工会前提交了约 700 个问题，其中薪酬问题最多，其次是要求董事会提高透明度。Kress 当场承诺，公司会照顾好每一位员工，让大家不必担心自己的薪酬待遇。

董事长 Harvey Jones 则再次明确，黄仁勋不会复职。他还首次在全员会上解释，董事会接受黄仁勋辞职，除了个人行为问题，还因为他「缺乏坦诚」。

Jones 表示，公司不可能找到「第二个黄仁勋」，但仍有具备技术能力、战略眼光和领导经验的人选。董事会不会为了尽快填补职位而降低标准，也欢迎员工推荐下一任 CEO 人选。

谷歌世界模型Genie 4向Ultra用户开放：AI世界能边玩边改，还能分享给其他人

Google DeepMind 将新一代世界模型 Genie 4 接入 Project Genie，开始向符合条件的 Google AI Ultra 订阅用户开放。Project Genie 是谷歌今年 1 月推出的网页应用，用户可以通过文字或图片创建虚拟世界，再用键盘控制角色，在 AI 实时生成的场景中自由探索。

Genie 4 加入了原生音频，能随着画面变化实时生成环境声、音乐和人物对话。用户还可以在探索过程中输入文字，随时改变天气、添加角色或触发事件，让虚拟世界按照自己的想法不断变化。

Project Genie 还新增了 AI 创作助手。之前用户需要自己描述场景、调整初始画面和视角，现在可以直接通过聊天设计世界，让 AI 自动生成初始场景和配乐。进入世界后，Gemini 还能持续观察画面，推荐下一步探索方向，甚至自动触发场景中的事件。

上一代 Genie 3 也获得升级，单次探索时长从 60 秒延长至 3 分钟，还能把多个虚拟世界连接起来，连续探索不同场景。用户也可以上传 360 度全景照片，让 AI 根据真实环境生成可探索的空间。

Project Genie 同时新增社区作品库，用户可以分享自己创建的世界，其他人可以直接进入探索，也能修改场景、音乐和规则，制作自己的版本。
